overview: The RC522 reads (and writes) the 13.56MHz RFID cards and key fobs used in countless access-control systems, transit cards, and hobby 'MIFARE Classic' tags, communicating with a microcontroller over SPI. Its single most important gotcha catches nearly every beginner at least once: unlike many sensor breakouts that tolerate a 5V logic bus, the RC522 chip itself is strictly 3.3V — running its SPI lines directly off a 5V Arduino without level shifting risks permanently damaging it, even though the module often works 'well enough' for a while before failing.
simpleSummary: A reader that can scan (and write to) RFID cards and key fobs, like the ones used for building access.

specifications.interface: SPI (also supports I2C/UART on some firmware, but SPI is standard)
specifications.cardTypes: MIFARE Classic, Ultralight, and similar 13.56MHz ISO 14443A tags

pinMap.name: SCK
pinMap.gotcha: Not 5V tolerant — connecting directly to a 5V Arduino's SPI pins without a level shifter risks damaging the chip over time.

pinMap.name: MOSI
pinMap.gotcha: Not 5V tolerant, same caution as SCK.

pinMap.name: IRQ
pinMap.function: Interrupt output, signals when a card enters the field (optional — most projects poll instead).

pinMap.name: 3.3V
pinMap.function: Power input — the module's only supported voltage.
pinMap.gotcha: Despite many tutorials showing it wired to an Arduino Uno's 5V pin (which works because they happen to only power it, not level-shift the data lines), the correct and safe supply is strictly 3.3V.

useCases.title: RFID access control / door lock
useCases.scenario: Grant access when a recognized card/tag is scanned, triggering a relay or solenoid lock.

useCases.title: Attendance/check-in system
useCases.scenario: Log timestamped check-ins as people scan personal RFID cards.

useCases.title: Inventory/asset tracking
useCases.scenario: Tag items with RFID stickers and scan them for inventory checks.

oftenConfusedWith: NFC modules (broader standard, RC522 covers the common MIFARE subset)
oftenUpgradedTo: PN532 (adds NFC peer-to-peer and card emulation modes)
